failures.criterion: 3a / the spec's Outcome - a denied issue-topic publish is named and counted instead of retried silently. It is not, for a notifying event, which is the shape a person's comment or a status change on a routed issue has: the issue topic itself is reported as "NATS is unreachable", the event is released with no attempt counted, the counter records reason="failed" where the denial belongs, no line names the issue subject, and the rest of that scan's backlog is abandoned. INFRA-749's alert, whose whole acceptance is matching this change's ERROR line, would not fire.
failures.evidence:
Cause: a publish window sends every destination of an event on one connection, and nats.go keeps one last error per connection (packages/envoy/internal/bus/async.go:248, w.conn.LastError()). publishDenial matches that one error against one subject (confirm.go:166-167), so only the destination whose violation the connection happened to keep is named a denial. Every other denied destination answers the acknowledgement timeout, becomes bus.ErrUnavailable, and settle's `case errors.Is(err, bus.ErrUnavailable)` arm (outbox/publisher.go:383-386) fires before `default: backOff`, releasing the event at INFO with no attempt counted; publishBatch then marks the batch unavailable (publisher.go:306-310) and the scan stops.

Red test: TestRunCountsEveryDeniedJetStreamDestinationOfOneEvent, packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox/core_denied_test.go, commit 538a6f5a18ff. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/outbox/ -run TestRunCountsEveryDeniedJetStreamDestinationOfOneEvent -count=3. Red 3 of 3 at head 7112831, the same line each time:
  core_denied_test.go:386: line "level=INFO msg=\"dispatch outbox: event released\" event_id=1 error=\"publish route \\\"session:33333333-...\\\": bus: NATS denied the publish to \\\"notifications.agent.33333333-...\\\": nats: permissions violation ... \\npublish owner topic \\\"notifications.dispatch.issue.T-1.issue.updated\\\": bus: NATS is unreachable: nats: timeout waiting for ack\"" reports a denied publish as an outage of the bus
The session route was named a denial and the issue topic - the subject this issue exists for - was named an outage. The rest of the package is green at the same commit (go test ./internal/dispatch/outbox/ -count=1: only this test fails, 173 s).

Same failure on the real surface, no test rig: envoy-dispatch built from head on a real nats-server 2.15.1 whose authorization is the production renderer's with notifications.> withheld, Postgres 17, at http://127.0.0.1:8848 (database d745two). Drove POST /api/v1/projects, POST /api/v1/issues, PATCH /api/v1/issues/TWO-1 with route session:33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333, then a person's comment through the dev sign-in cookie (POST /api/v1/issues/TWO-1/comments as alice@example.com, notify true). After 30 s: `select id, type, notify, attempt_count from events` gives comment.created notify=t attempt_count=0, and issue.created and issue.updated also 0 behind it, while the one single-destination event ahead of them counted 1; GET /metrics reads reason="failed" 19 beside reason="denied" 6. On the same binary and server a single-destination event counts its attempts normally (stack 8846, DEN-1: attempt_count 14, reason="denied" only, no "NATS is unreachable" line).

Achievable: nats.go hands every violation to the connection's async error handler with its own subject (packages/envoy/internal/bus/connect.go:296-315, which already forwards to asyncErrCB), so a per-subject record of the violations seen on the connection is available to publishDenial in place of the single LastError(). The design is the implementer's; the test pins the observable contract (every denied destination counted as a denial, the attempt counted, no outage line), not the mechanism.

failures.criterion: The pull request's and the plan's stated contract for INFRA-749 is not pinned by the test that is said to pin it. The plan (task 2) and the body state the alert's matcher as level ERROR and msg `dispatch outbox: publish event` and an `error` containing `NATS denied the publish`, and the plan says of task 3's test: "A later edit that reworded any of the three would break the deployment's alert silently; this test is what stops it."
failures.evidence: TestRunRetriesAnIssueTopicNATSDenies (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox/core_denied_test.go:312-326) scans the buffer for a line containing `dispatch outbox: publish event` and then requires only the issue subject and `Permissions Violation for Publish`, which is nats-server's own wording. It asserts neither `level=ERROR` nor `NATS denied the publish` (the text of bus.ErrPublishDenied, confirm.go:16) nor the `event_id` the plan names. slog.Error at backOff (publisher.go:395) lowered to Warn or Info, or a reword of ErrPublishDenied, leaves this test and every other test in the repository green while the deployed alert stops matching: a grep of packages/ finds `NATS denied the publish` asserted in exactly one other place, attempt_test.go:219, an error-wrapping unit test that would catch the reword but not the level. Add the three missing assertions to that test, as the plan states them; this round wrote no test for it because the same file is where the first failure is fixed.

notFindings: renderInbound's skip rule is safe for every wire value: quiet true skips, false shows, absent falls back to notify, and null, a string, a number or an object all show. The Go outbox marshals a plain bool with no omitempty (publisher.go:1268-1272), so only true and false reach a reader, and no value hides a frame a reader needs.
Broker.Notify's answer is unchanged for every event type and actor: Quiet's arms reproduce each of the base function's early returns, and the events suite is green.

(*nats.Conn).LastError() is nil-receiver safe (nats.go v1.50.0 nats.go:4033-4036, returning ErrInvalidConnection), so Client.lastError on a client with no connection cannot panic and publishDenial answers nil for it.

parseDispatchFrame's read of quiet in the targeted branch cannot change behaviour today: the two producers of the {event, delivery} shape (api/comment_delivery.go:440-450 and api/message_delivery.go:543-552) wrap a bare model.Event, which carries no quiet, and those frames reach a session on its own agent subject, which the DISPATCH_TOPIC_PREFIX guard excludes from the skip. It is a forward-compatible read kept in step with the untargeted branch, not a defect.
GET /metrics exposes three lines and nothing sensitive.
forArchitect: The round fails on the first entry of `failures`: the denial classification holds only while an event has one JetStream destination, and a notifying event on a routed issue has two, where the issue topic itself is reported as an unreachable bus and the backlog stalls. It is this change's own code path, it is reproduced both by a red test in the repository's suite and on the real surface with the rendered production grants, and the fix is available through the connection's async error handler, which already carries each violation's own subject. The second entry is smaller: the ERROR line INFRA-749 is blocked on is not pinned by the test the plan and the body say pins it. No product, scope or design decision is open, so there is nothing here for a person to answer.
